rows.gloss: to make the first haircut for a child
rows.etymology: 1080. Bng. bɔ̀drɛṇɔ ‘to make the first haircut for a child’, Jaun. bhadar karnȭ ‘to shave the head’, Ku. bhadra karnō ‘to shave’ (but according to Sharma [1983: 130] it has the meaning ‘shaving of head on account of death of some elderly close blood relation’)< OIA bhadrākaraṇa- ‘shaving’ (9381) with modern reflexes in P. and M. to which are to ͡ be added Bhad. bhʌḍḷ ‘shaving of the head etc. in mourning’, Kal. ṣiṣ badaváv ‘barber’ and ṣiṣ badék, budí kárik, budían tyek all ‘to cut someone’s hair’ — M.wār. bhadər ‘to shave’, bhaddaṇ ‘shaving of the head at the death of one’s relative’ — Kh. baḍkeʔ ‘coiffure’. Also here is an example of the repeated recreation of morphemes/concepts based on old remembered linguistic patterns. Note: Wg. brã̄- ‘to shave, shear’ and G.pars. borkũ ‘completely shaven’ (which is a past participle) have perhaps another origin and may be compared with OCS britva ‘razor, Russian Church Slavonic briju, briti ‘to shave’, perhaps with Thracian βρίλων ‘barber’ (see also Katičič [1976: 139]), and Mallory and Adams’ reconstruction PIE bʰrehxi- ‘destroy, cut to pieces’ (Pokorny has ‘cut with s.th. sharp’ [IEW: 166]).
